newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up in Oct 98, otherwise quiet, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up in Oct 98, otherwise quiet, rangebound.

text.p: UK natural gas prices were mostly unchanged in rangebound trade on Tuesday although there was a slight rise in October 1997, traders and brokers said.
One trader reported buying 200,000 therms a day of gas in October in four separate deals, all between 10.80 and 10.90 pence a therm. But most other periods were little changed.
"Basically it's been pretty much a rangebound day," said a trader. "The market's been staying where it was yesterday," said another.

There was active trade on October futures as well as on the physical market, and January and February futures were also higher, even though these months did not trade on the OTC market. One dealer said there was a clear relationship between developments on the two markets.
"OTC offers were being pulled when futures trades were going up. I would say it's one of the few days when people were swivelling their heads from one to the other," the dealer said.
But another dealer was not convinced by the significance of higher futures prices in the winter.
"At the end of the day someone could be playing games," he said. "25,000 therms a day won't move the market even if they go through the offer."

Trade was done reasonably far forward, with deals seen for Q4 98 and the gas year 98 - as far as September 1999 - as well as the calendar year 1998. But the focus was the period covering September and October this year, with little interest seen in the coming winter, in contrast with recent days.

One of the largest players in the market in recent days reported doing no deals at all. And the whole market had a quiet, subdued tone even though futures were unusually active, with 310 lots traded at mostly higher prices.
